# dsh-zen-remote

> One DeepSeek Harness plugin, two roles, shipped as ONE npm package. The **host** role: app-shell mobile UI (two-level page stack, session-list home, reworked composer, gestures, phone-local attachment upload), pairing-code/device-token gateway for public-internet access behind your own reverse proxy, installable PWA, real Web Push, and per-session sharing to paired desktops. The **client** role: runs inside another DSH desktop app and surfaces the host's remote-enabled sessions in its own sidebar — history, live progress, messages, approvals, terminals; everything executes on the host over zen-remote's relay protocol.

## Key facts
- One npm package `dsh-zen-remote`, MIT. Install: `dsh plugin add dsh-zen-remote` (or one dependency line in `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop|web/package.json` + `pnpm install`), then restart DSH. The composition layer is a single row `dsh-zen-remote`; the main entry loads the gateway and push sub-plugins itself according to the `role` config. Old `dsh-zen-remote-gateway` / `dsh-zen-remote-push` rows are warned and skipped — do not re-add them (a second gateway would fight over port 3088).
- Roles: `role: host` (default) runs mobile UI + gateway child + push + session sharing + the relay server; `role: client` runs the relay client and the sidebar/session-page remote parts only — no gateway, no push, no phone UI. Anything that is not exactly `client` degrades to host.
- Config lives in the DSH Plugins page settings block; per field the first legal value wins: environment variable > plugin row settings > `~/.dsh/lan-gate.config.json` > default. Restart-required fields (`role`, `port`, `host`, `targetPort`, `rateLimit`, `trustedProxies`, `vapidSubject`, `lang`, push fields) reload the plugin row automatically; everything else is volatile and read live.
- Host sharing: per-session remote toggle from three places (sidebar context menu, title-row icon with confirm, settings list); idle sleep after 48h without session activity (running/waiting sessions exempt, viewers don't count); auto-share new sessions (opt-in; relay-created sessions always auto-share); subagent/fork sessions follow the parent.
- Pairing codes are role-bound: web app devices (phones/browsers, see all sessions) redeem on the pairing page; desktop app devices pair from the client's settings page via `/lan-gate/pair/claim-desktop` and only ever reach the relay prefix (everything else 403 `relay-only`).
- Relay protocol (prefix `/_dsh/zen-remote/relay`): `GET ping`, `POST v1/handshake` (relay protocol version + DSH interface fingerprints — version mismatch refuses; fingerprint mismatch annotates and degrades; the answer carries `serverName`/`deviceName`), `POST v1/invoke`, `POST v1/stream` (NDJSON, ping heartbeats that carry the current `serverName`/`deviceName`, `unshared` error line on close), `POST v1/event-result`, `POST v1/http` (the plain-HTTP long tail: only `changes.summary` / `changes.diff`, GET only, query normalized to `sessionId`/`seq`/`index`, dispatched in-process through the host's shared `/api` handler), `POST v1/upload` (a remote session's non-image attachments: raw byte stream, share-checked, query normalized to `sessionId`/`name`, 100 MiB cap answers 413, 8 concurrent per device answers 429, dispatched in-process through the same shared handler), `POST v1/unshare`, `POST v1/device/name` (gateway-handled rename of the CALLING device's own record — paired desktop clients only, never forwarded to DSH; 1–40 chars). Access control is a per-method allowlist (`src/relay-access.ts` RELAY_METHODS, mirrored by intercept.ts CLIENT_METHOD_FIELDS, pinned identical by test); global reads (`session/control`, `session/list`, `workspace/follow`) and the @-mention candidates are output-filtered (candidates list only shared sessions); `session/modelCatalog` is a parameter-less global read whose `failures` array the server empties; `dsh-session:` references are scanned wherever DSH would inject them — prompt content, queue-edit content, every string of a `commands/execute` call — and a reference naming an unshared session refuses the call. Approval/question events forward first come, first served; the relay never answers on the client's behalf (an unshared session's approval waits for the server UI or the next subscription), and unshared sessions' notification-type events are never forwarded.
- Remote extras (T51/T52): a remote session can attach non-image files — the sub-client's own backend wraps the host's `fetchRoutes` upload entry and streams the bytes through `v1/upload` (the 100 MiB cap is the relay's own, an over-limit pick is refused locally on the client, slow links are bounded by a 300 s client-side timeout; export is disabled remotely instead — menu item hidden, backend 403 for virtual ids). The model picker in a remote session lists the SERVER's catalog (groups named "server name · group name"); local sessions list only local models, the last server groups survive relay offline, and virtual groups never appear in local settings such as the vision router (boundary: a server-created session that never sent a message shows the local default model).
- Gateway auth chain: device token (Bearer) → gateway marker headers `x-zen-remote-via/-role/-device` + `x-zen-remote-secret` (per-load shared secret, `LAN_GATE_RELAY_SECRET`, not externally settable, re-verified with timingSafeEqual) → per-method share-table check. Admin API stays loopback-only; forwarded requests may read status but never mutate.
- Admin surface: the dsh-zen-remote settings block (pairing with role picker, device list with rename/set-role/revoke, push test, shares list). `/lan-gate/admin` is now just a notice pointing there.
- Trust model: a paired desktop client is a TRUSTED DEVICE — server-user terminal without sandbox/approval gates, file previews not contained to the session dir, session creation in any workspace. "Shared only" constrains session data (lists, history, events are refused/filtered server-side; @ candidates list only shared sessions; references in messages, queue edits and slash commands naming an unshared session refuse the call), not the machine.
- Env: `LAN_GATE_PORT` (3088), `LAN_GATE_HOST`, `LAN_GATE_TARGET_PORT` (auto-discovered), `LAN_GATE_RATE_LIMIT` (120), `LAN_GATE_TRUSTED_PROXIES`, `LAN_GATE_VAPID_SUBJECT`, `LAN_GATE_LANG`, `LAN_GATE_RELAY_SECRET` (auto), `DSH_PUSH_*`, `DSH_PUSH_APPROVAL_GRACE_MS`. Same keys (lowerCamelCase) in `lan-gate.config.json`.
- Security: 8-char one-time role-bound pairing code (10 min TTL), 5-wrong-code lockout, revocable per-device tokens (kills connections + push subscription), 120 req/min per client IP for unpaired requests.
- Known limits: remote sessions disable export (menu item hidden, backend 403 for virtual ids); changes summary/diff work remotely but the "open on the server machine" entries (open / reveal in Finder / open in app) are hidden there; with dsh-better-sidebar installed, its file surfaces (file browser, editor, git, tasks, bottom workbench, floating windows) are hidden in remote sessions because they act on the CLIENT machine's own files — so remote sessions have no sidebar file browser (it takes over the host's "Files" tab) and file links in chat or deliverables open an empty right column; @ candidates are truncated to 50 by the host BEFORE share filtering (a shared session can be missing from the list on a session-heavy server); third-party plugins' non-standard endpoints are not forwarded — their tools run on the server and are unaffected, what breaks is UI calling the plugin's own backend with a session id (better-sidebar, handled as above); both ends need zen-remote 2.0.x; server switch-back or workspace-id reuse needs a page reload; several DSH windows at once (including the desktop backend opened in a browser) can misjudge which session is currently open — closed-remote hiding can fire at the wrong moment and worst case dismiss an open session to the home page. Dev only (see AGENTS.md hard constraints): same-machine testing must reach the gateway over a LAN IP (loopback = local-direct, skips token checks) — normal two-machine use is unaffected.
